text: Why must the width of a stored value be fixed in advance?
choices: Variable-width values cannot represent negative numbers
It buys constant-time addressing and lets arithmetic be built from finite hardware
Fixed width removes the possibility of overflow
The JVM specification forbids variable-width data
explanation: If values vary in length, finding the n-th means walking the n−1 before it — linear instead of constant time — and an adder is a physical arrangement with a specific number of columns that cannot stretch. The answer about overflow inverts the truth: fixed width is precisely what creates overflow rather than preventing it.
